list.title: Databases
list.description: Databases {appName} protects by address and user, without backing up the whole server.
list.loadError: The databases could not be loaded

noTenant.title: No tenant selected
noTenant.description: Choose a tenant at the top to see its databases.

empty.title: No database yet
empty.description: Enter an address and a user. {appName} recognises the engine, shows what the user allows, and only then saves.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Each connection is one instance or one SQLite file with its sign-in, executor and schedule.
connections.name: Connection

suggestions.title: Found, not protected
suggestions.description: The agents of your machines found these databases. A connection exists only once you test and save it.
suggestions.noPort: Runs in a container without a published port; enter the address yourself.

add.title: Add database
add.description: An address, a user and a password are enough. Test the connection; it is saved only after that.
add.addressHint: A URL (postgresql://, mysql://, mariadb://, sqlserver://), host:port, only the host, or the path of an SQLite file. A user and password in the URL move into their fields.
add.executorHint: Who opens the connection: the {appName} server itself (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB) or an agent in the database's network. SQLite and SQL Server need an agent on their own machine.
add.socket: Sign in over the local socket, without a password
add.socketHint: Only with an agent on the database machine: PostgreSQL as postgres (peer), MariaDB and MySQL as root.
add.userHint: A backup user of its own is recommended; an admin user works too.
add.unencrypted: Connect unencrypted when the server offers no TLS
add.unencryptedHint: The notice stays with the connection. The {appName} server never connects to a public address without TLS.
add.waiting: The agent is testing the connection
add.waitingHint: It picks the test up at its next contact, within about five minutes. You can keep this window open.
add.expired: The agent did not report for 15 minutes. Check that it runs, or choose another executor.
add.name: Name
add.nameHint: Without one, the connection is named after its address.
add.modeHint: Point-in-time and the warm copy follow in later releases.
add.selectionHint: Databases added later are included automatically.

probe.databases: {count, plural, one {# database found} other {# databases found}}
probe.identityUnknown: This user cannot read the identity of the instance; a change of instance would then go unnoticed.
probe.schemasByName: Schemas are recognised by their name: a schema dropped and created again under the same name counts as the same one.

capabilities.verifyOnInstance: Check and restore on the same instance

notes.pg_before_14: Before PostgreSQL 14 the right to read every object cannot be checked in advance.
notes.pg_hba_unchecked: {appName} cannot see the replication entry in pg_hba.conf with this user.
notes.sqlserver_later: SQL Server is still backed up by the native backup on the machine's page.
notes.grants_truncated: The server's list of grants was too long to read in full, so missing rights cannot be determined reliably.

admin.title: Admin user
admin.description: This user may do everything ({rights}). {appName} only needs the rights of the backup user below.

grant.missing: These statements create a backup user restow_backup with exactly the missing rights:
grant.recommended: Recommended: a backup user restow_backup with exactly these rights:
grant.savesAnyway: You can save the connection anyway; it can then do what the user allows.

intervals.minutes: {count, plural, =15 {every 15 minutes} =30 {every 30 minutes} =60 {hourly} =120 {every 2 hours} =240 {every 4 hours} =360 {every 6 hours} =720 {every 12 hours} =1440 {daily} other {every # minutes}}

executor.agentOffline: Agent on {hostname}, no contact for more than 15 minutes

connection.loadError: The connection could not be loaded
connection.socket: Over the local socket, without a password
connection.credentialSet: User and password are stored encrypted
connection.databasesDescription: A database dropped and created again under the same name is another database with a history of its own.
connection.deleteDescription: The connection, its databases and the stored credentials are deleted. Type the name to confirm.

confirm.tlsDescription: The server shows another certificate than the confirmed one. Until you confirm it, {appName} does not connect again. Check the fingerprint:
confirm.tlsQuestion: Confirm only if you know the certificate was renewed. The confirmation is recorded in the audit log.
confirm.instanceDescription: Another instance answers under the address, for example after a move or a failover. {appName} does not keep backing up silently.
confirm.instanceQuestion: Confirm that the new instance has the same job. Its databases get a history of their own; the old instance's stays separate. The confirmation is recorded in the audit log.
confirm.fromHealth: The health check sees it and did not sign in for it. Test the connection ("Test connection") to confirm it afterwards.

settings.title: Settings
settings.credentialsHint: Leave empty to keep the stored credentials. Stored credentials are never shown.

database.loadError: The database could not be loaded
database.identityKnown: By the database's name and id

noBackups.title: No backup yet
noBackups.description: Backups and check reports appear here once the database is backed up.

codes.db_engine_changed: Another engine answers under the address
codes.db_instance_changed: Another instance answers under the address
codes.db_target_is_restow: This is the database of this {appName} installation
codes.db_not_a_database: No known database answers under the address
codes.db_engine_unsupported: This engine needs an agent on its own machine
codes.db_auth_unsupported: The sign-in over the socket is not possible here
codes.db_warm_copy_name_taken: Name already taken on the target
codes.db_run_overlap: Run skipped, the previous one was still running

problems.generic: That did not work. Try again.
problems.executor: This executor cannot open the connection.
problems.db_private_network: The address is in a private network or is a container name. Only a provider admin can approve it for the {appName} server; an agent in that network can reach it.
problems.db_forbidden_address: The address is link-local or reserved (such as a cloud's metadata service). The {appName} server never connects there.
problems.probe-required: Test the connection before you save it.
problems.tls-missing: The server offers no TLS. Tick the box for unencrypted connections to save it anyway.
problems.target-is-restow: This is the database of this {appName} installation. It is protected by the installation's backup, not in this module.
problems.name-taken: Another connection already has this name.
problems.probe-limit: Too many tests in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
problems.probe-busy: Other tests are running. Try again in a moment.
problems.credentials-required: Enter the password again: stored credentials only go to the executor they were stored for.
problems.own-database-unknown: The {appName} server cannot tell right now where its own database is, so it tests no connections. Try again in a moment.
problems.confirm: There is nothing to confirm. Test the connection again.
problems.server-connection-limit: This tenant already runs as many connections on the {appName} server as allowed. Run this connection on an agent.
problems.run-active: This connection is running a backup or a restore right now. Try again when it has ended.
problems.restore-name: The new database's name is too long (at most 63 bytes).
problems.backup-gone: This backup is no longer available.
problems.restore-target: Choose a connection of the same engine.

health.title: Health checks
health.description: {appName} checks the connection {count, plural, one {every minute} other {every # minutes}} with the backup user, read-only, as its executor sees it.
health.notMonitoring: No replacement for monitoring: it measures only what the backup needs.

now.label: Now
now.never: No check yet. The first follows within the connection's interval, for an agent with its next heartbeat.
now.failing: {count, plural, one {One check} other {# checks in a row}} failed since {since}
now.alerted: The alert "Database not reachable" was sent; "reachable again" follows with the first success.
now.paused: The connection is switched off; no health checks run.

latency.title: Response time
latency.description: Connection, TLS, sign-in and SELECT 1, mean and maximum per interval
latency.summary: Response time in the period: last {last}, at most {max}.

connections.title: Connections in use
connections.description: Maximum per interval against the instance's max_connections
connections.summary: Connections in the period: last {used} of {max}.

empty.title: No checks in this period
empty.description: Once the executor checks the connection, response time and connections appear here.

health.loadError: The health check history could not be loaded

band.label: Reachability of the last 24 hours
band.summary: Last 24 hours: {ok} hours reachable, {problem} with outages, {none} without a check.

size.title: Size per day
size.description: Read at most once an hour; the last value of each day.

empty.title: No size yet
empty.description: The health checks read the size at most once an hour.

size.loadError: The size history could not be loaded

backups.title: Backups
backups.description: Every backup is a snapshot of its own in the connection's repository. Unverified until the check in the verification service arrives.
backups.queued: The backup is planned. It appears here once it is done.
backups.none: No backup yet. The first one comes with the connection's schedule or with “Back up now”.
backups.restoreDescription: {appName} always creates a new database and restores the backup into it. An existing database is never overwritten.
backups.restoreNameHint: Leave empty for the suggestion. At most 63 bytes; the name must not be taken.
backups.restoreNameInvalid: The name is too long, contains control characters or starts or ends with a blank.
backups.restoreOwners: Owners and privileges are not carried over. The restore guide describes how to set them up.
backups.restoreOtherConnection: The executor of the target connection receives the content of this one backup through {appName}, not the source connection's repository.
backups.globalsDescription: The instance's roles, with their password hashes where the user could read them. Administrators only; every download is logged.
